hints: Look at the functional group in the monomer, the C=C double bond tells you exactly what type of polymerisation this will be.
Remember that in addition polymerisation the double bond opens to a single bond, but all the other atoms stay exactly where they were.
Draw the monomer as $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ and join the two alkene carbons into the backbone, then see which side chain is left hanging off.
walkthrough:
**Identify the polymerisation type**

This monomer, $\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCH}_2\text{OH}$, contains a C=C alkene bond. That means it undergoes addition polymerisation, not condensation.

Rule for addition:
$$\text{C=C} \rightarrow \text{-C-C- backbone with same side groups}$$

**Open the double bond**

Break the pi bond in $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-$ to give two single-bonded backbone carbons. Nothing is lost, no small molecule is removed.

$$\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCH}_2\text{OH} \rightarrow \text{-[CH}_2\text{-CH(CH}_2\text{OH)]-}$$

**Check the repeat unit**

The backbone must be two carbons long, with the whole $-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ group still intact as a side chain on every second carbon. That matches only one of the given structures, so that is the repeat unit.

options.A: Incorrect. This looks like a condensation or ether type unit with O in the backbone. Addition polymerisation never puts oxygen into the main chain and never loses atoms from the monomer.
options.B: Correct. Opening the $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-$ double bond gives a $-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}-$ backbone, with the $-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ group unchanged as the side chain. This uses all atoms of $\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCH}_2\text{OH}$ with no double bond left.
options.C: Incorrect. This still contains a C=C double bond in the backbone. In addition polymerisation the pi bond is always broken to form two new single C-C links to neighbours.
options.D: Incorrect. This has a three-carbon backbone with $-\text{OH}$ directly attached. The monomer has only two alkene carbons for the backbone, and the side group must be the full $-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, not just $-\text{OH}$.
